Dear Mrs. Okafor, I'm not sure you'll remember me, but I was in your 11th grade English class a long time ago. I was the kid in the back who never turned in the reading journal on time. I've been meaning to write this for years, and I'm finally just doing it. You were the first teacher who ever told me my writing was worth reading. There was this essay I threw together the night before, and you wrote a note at the bottom that said something like, This is the most honest thing you've written. Keep going. And I kept that paper in a shoebox all through college and through two moves across country. I ended up becoming a reporter. And now I edit a little paper in the town where I live. And every time some young writer comes into my office, all nervous and apologizing for the draft, I think about that note and I try to do for them what you did for me. I don't think teachers hear enough about how things turn out, so I just wanted you to know. Thank you for paying attention to a kid who really wasn't making it easy.
